**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

- **Section 20(d)** bars any assignment without the other party's written consent, with no affiliate/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard. That fails the fallback and is effectively the playbook's walk-away case (blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out).
- **Section 3(c)** reinforces the bar against us specifically, allowing transfer only as Garman authorizes in writing.
- **No change-of-control provision exists**, and Section 17's termination triggers are notice/insolvency-based only — so there is no Garman exit or re-pricing right on our change of control to delete.

Redline (validated, ok:true) adds our affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice, applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments, prohibits Garman assigning to a competitor of ours, and conforms Section 3(c) by cross-reference.
